themes_detail.label: Unleashed dogs surge
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 6 reports THIS WEEK, a 500% increase versus the 1.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden enforcement gap or behavioral shift in a dense neighborhood with limited dog parks.
evidence: 6 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.07, high severity)
500% spike represents statistically significant deviation from 8-week pattern
Greenpoint/Williamsburg has high residential density and limited off-leash areas
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept and NYPD about enforcement; talk to dog owners and residents about recent neighborhood changes
Investigate whether recent weather, events, or social media organizing has driven dog-walking behavior shifts

themes_detail.label: Street lights failing rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Street Light Condition complaints jumped to 34 reports THIS WEEK versus a 13.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 152% spike—suggesting possible infrastructure failure, contractor issues, or power distribution problems affecting public safety in Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: 34 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.54, high severity)
152% spike in single week suggests acute failure rather than chronic underinvestment
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for infrastructure improvement
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and ConEd for outage maps, maintenance schedules, and root cause
Document dark corridors with photos/video; interview residents about safety concerns, especially post-fatal bus crash coverage

themes_detail.label: Pigeon infestations spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary Pigeon Condition complaints hit 3 reports THIS WEEK, a 700% spike versus the 0.4 weekly baseline, indicating a sudden pest control or waste management failure that may signal broader sanitation breakdown.
evidence: 3 pigeon complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, high severity)
Correlates with 'Dirty Condition' complaints remaining elevated (663 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations; contact NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene and Parks Dept about pest control deployment
Interview residents about food waste management, restaurant dumpster practices, and timing of spike

themes_detail.label: Root and sewer damage widening
themes_detail.summary: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints surged 9 reports 2 weeks ago—a 350% increase versus the 2.0 weekly baseline—suggesting systemic underground infrastructure deterioration that may worsen into street collapses or flooding.
evidence: 9 root/sewer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.29, high severity)
350% spike matches recurring CB budget request for DEP capital investment
Precursor signal to potential sinkholes, flooding, or building foundation damage
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection for aging sewer atlas, recent main breaks, and inspection backlogs in CD 301
Document visible sidewalk buckling, tree root exposure; interview homeowners about basement water intrusion claims

themes_detail.label: Tree planting interest explodes
themes_detail.summary: New Tree Request complaints spiked to 3 reports last week—a 2300% increase versus the 0.1 weekly baseline—potentially reflecting organized community advocacy, developer mitigation commitments, or emerging green-space activism following recent rezoning proposals.
evidence: 3 tree requests last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, high severity)
2300% spike is single largest statistical anomaly in dataset
5 active ULURPs and 1322 building permits filed in 90 days may trigger environmental mitigation demands
reporting_angles: Identify the 3 complainants; determine if they're organized via community group, social media, or responding to developer commitments
Investigate tree canopy loss from recent construction and Parks Dept backlog for replacement planting
